decision: Retain original 0.6-second capture policy for both voices. No production DSP change was made by this experiment.
reason: Longer ROLL captures improve the strongest periodic spectral-line offset at C2 but trade phase-window detector refusals into another low note. No candidate was a clear improvement across the bounded transition matrix.
method: One-file scratch Kotlin overlays, compiled with K2JVMCompiler 2.0.21 targeting JVM 17, loaded before the real compiled production classes. Public Skirl APIs ran the actual 4x capture and shared output conditioning. No production source file was edited.

candidates.base06: Original min(.60, .30 * rollingDuration) target; unchanged production code.
candidates.rollnote09: ROLL only: min(.90, .60 * max(1, 130.8/hz), .60 * rollingDuration); WHIRR original. Scratch voice identification uses disjoint calibrated launch-angle domains, not a proposed production API.
candidates.rollnote12: ROLL only: min(1.20, .60 * max(1, 130.8/hz), .60 * rollingDuration); WHIRR original. Same scratch voice identification.
candidates.quantization: The 130.8 Hz reference is the scratch approximation to Keys.midiHz(48). Every tested hop rounds to the same note-cycle count as the exact reference. These were research candidates, not shipped macro mappings.

detectorRefusalExplanation.rule: The smallest interior autocorrelation peak must exceed 0.85 times the global maximum. A smooth low note can have its global maximum at the shortest-lag endpoint, which is not a fundamental-period peak.
detectorRefusalExplanation.interpretation: The failing window has substantial near-root periodic content. The constrained known-target peak is diagnostic, not a replacement for the actual detector or evidence of perceived pitch.

normalizedCycleWindows.starts: i * actualCycleSeconds / 12, i=0..11; log start display rounds to two decimals
